Your maximum margin there is 0.8 K, P about 0.57-0.61.

'Your headline is a TIM and clamp-pressure story.' The 28.4/33.3 K headline uses PCM at 25 psi (2 kN), which no real package allows (4-12 psi). It is also about 1.5 K optimistic, because you subtracted our calibration-absorbed 2-D penalty; corrected it is 29.9/34.8 K. Put LM on an incumbent split-flow plate and you get about 27.4/35.3 K, which beats PRISM+PCM on the average with no new manufacturing.

'You beat a deliberately standard demonstrator, not our best.' CoolIT's brief says the goal was to show that 'standard coldplate designs and standard system operation' suffice. A 7-part, 6-interface bespoke stack beating it says nothing about OMNI (> 300 W/cm2, 'up to 60 % lower R') or our 2027 product, which we will publish in the OCP format we wrote.

'Your dP win evaporates at the system boundary.' At the tray loop with UQD08s it is 40-49 vs 56-79 kPa. Against 80-180 kPa of rack and CDU head it is about 7-19 % of loop head and about US$44k/yr of pump energy per 100 MW. In mixed racks you must throttle it away with orifices. Your dP 'reconstruction' of our plate also disagrees by 3-8x with published GB300 plate dP.

'You lose the only other point we published.' At our 4 kW, 25 cm2 point PRISM's drop-in core is 0.0096-0.0109 C/W against < 0.009, and up to 28 % worse on a 20 cm2 heater. Your reconstruction misses that datum by ≥ 37 %, so every model-only 'CoolIT-like' comparison is model against model: the GPU class, 350 W/cm2, the flow sweep, Q capacity and inlet headroom.

'Split-Flow, plainly.' A 0.3 mm kerf does not end the inter-fin passage: about 49 % of inflow enters through fin tips under the window, between the channel's ends. The kerf is worth 2.6 % of cell dT (an insubstantial difference), and your stamped plates and seals supply '513's plate-and-seal element. Your US beachhead ships in 2028 while the 2008 family is live, and Taiwan manufacture runs into TW I606224. Your own marketing says PRISM 'removes split-flow's ramp' by doing split flow every 12 mm.

Segment-level maldistribution is actually 1.23-1.43 (max/min), and the 18-line layout leaves dead-end fin strips over the heater edge that run 10-15 K hot.

'You cannot inspect your own critical joint.' An unbonded land strip passes proof, the flatness scan, the IR screen, dP, sample burst and your E1 gate. The plenum stamping route (web/t 0.33) cannot be built.

'Your fouling story is worse than ours, and invisible.' A 0.15 mm gap behind 50 um absolute gives about 7 years of exclusion life, against 15 years for a 0.2 mm gap, from your own model. Port dP is 82 % inertial, so fin fouling barely moves it: +6 % plate dP for a 10 um deposit. The plate is passive with no field signature, and the operator finds out from GPU throttling.

(NVIDIA thermal architect) 'Why would we switch the Rubin/Feynman socket?' GPU-class average is parity (-0.2 to -0.5 K with a lid) and the maximum gain is +1.7-2.4 K. Your own section 6.4 says dP is not a differentiator. Per-plate cost is +17-35 % even after cost-down. It needs a tray filter, and the 1.74 kg plate puts 510-850 N of shock load on the package. We buy a standardised design centrally, so a Group-A house cannot insert it. Our roadmap is moving to micro-channel lids and MLCP, for which you have no design numbers.

(NVIDIA thermal architect) 'Where is your transient analysis?' A 1.0/0.8 mm base halves near-die heat capacity against a 2 mm base (0.34 vs 0.69 J/K/cm2; diffusion about 9 vs 36 ms). Under millisecond-to-second power excursions the case-temperature overshoot is unknown, and so is the throttling behaviour.

'Your 350 W/cm2 margin is mislabeled.' The split-flow 88.6 K uses paste 0.07, not 0.05. Like-for-like the margin is about 18-20 K, not 27-28 K. Your P-grade reaches about 87 C and misses 85 C. And your heaters are rated 155 W/cm2, so you cannot test it.

'Your capacity claims exceed your own rules and rigs.' The 26.4, 23.3 and 34.1 kW capacities need 28-41 LPM, which breaks your 1.5 m/s port and 2.0 m/s meter caps. Your TTV stops at 18 kW and your rig at 25 kW. The 'equal pumping power' row at 28.5 LPM also exceeds the meter cap.

'Two-phase already beats your headroom.' Accelsius publishes 54 C inlet as equivalent to single-phase at 45 C (+9 K) and -9 C Tj on B200. Corrected like-for-like, PRISM gives +5.8-7 K at P50 and +2-3 K at P90, and your facility value case (15-60x) collapses to about 2-10x for 15 kW and inverts for the GPU class.

'Your liquid-metal tier is not engineered for the field.' Galinstan freezes at about -19 C, inside your -40 C storage cycle. Ga embrittles the Al frames your own team proposes. No LM reliability data exist above about 10 cm2. A '5-year inspection FRU' is incompatible with GPU module RMA practice.

'You cannot claim a win on a spec you have not read.' The OCP recommended TIM, case definition, dP boundary and filtration rating are all unread, and you mis-date the spec. Your class-A 'must beat' rule is undefined until you do. You are also measuring in OCP format against our non-OCP brief, which mixes protocols.

'Your moat disappears the day you publish.' The full OCP report discloses the architecture, and filings 2-4 are anticipated or obvious (verify-ip). Nidec's WO2026100588 is already industrialising fin-tip-brazed covers. AVC and Auras already ship MLCP at 30-33 % gross margin with 40-50 % share. Ecolab, our parent, sells the loop chemistry and filtration your fine channels depend on.

'Your sustainability and compliance story is missing.' Your wetted path uses PTFE and your LM dam uses FKM, fluoropolymers kept in scope by ECHA RAC (Mar 2026). You give no IEC/UL 62368-1 liquid-filled-component plan, no water-use number, and no heat-reuse claim, though your headroom would allow about 62-65 C return water, which EnEfG/EED customers value.

final-architect.headline: PRISM-15 Rev A is the design of record: the gap-closer's PKG-A lean stack, plus four fixes made in this revision. The fixes are a skirted drawn cap (one external perimeter seam), a stepped metered grate (jets land on the grate lip, not on the fins), a doubled outlet header with a 0.5 kPa outlet orifice row (segment max/min 1.06), and a mandatory supplied 33 um tray cartridge. Every number was re-run with each plate's own 2-D penalty and PG25 conductivity corrected to 0.49 W/mK. Against CoolIT on the same paste class: 31.0/38.7 K vs 34.4/44.2 K (-10 %/-12 %). On PCM: 29.1/34.8 K. Plate dP is 7.6 kPa vs about 22 kPa reconstructed; height 20.8 mm; mass 1.24 kg. Rev A wins on uniformity, capacity (+22-25 %), inlet headroom (+5.5 K at P50) and the maximum at every OCP flow. It costs US$165 vs US$126 per plate (+31 %); cost per kW is at parity, or 6-9 % better with the E1-gated C2 Cu-Sn belt route (US$144). It openly concedes the low-flow average, the 100 cm2 average, the 4 kW drop-in point, field record and fouling life at equal filtration. The 12-month programme costs US$8.4-10.7 M and is gated in tranches. P(decisive PCM result at M12) is about 0.43.

changes_from_draft: Every absolute number now carries PRISM's own 2-D penalty and PG25 k = 0.49 (verify-physics). The draft core moves from 28.4/33.3 to 29.9/34.8 K on PCM. Rev A is 29.1/34.8 K on PCM and 31.0/38.7 K on paste.

PKG-A is adopted as Rev A: a metered grate (meter merged into the grate), a folded 0.8 mm Cu plenum (replaces the refuted 4.5 mm stamped laminations), an arched drawn cap (replaces the forged bar and removes its stack-up error), graded 5 mm plenums, L 7.7 mm with 15 lines (fixes the 18-line edge error), and a 0.8 mm base gated on E1. Height goes from 26.4 to 20.8 mm, mass from 1.74 to 1.24 kg, cost from US$209 to US$165.

New in this revision: (a) a skirted cap, so there is one external perimeter seam instead of six; (b) a stepped-recess grate, so jets land on the grate lip, which keeps the 0.5 m/s fin-entry cap, protects the base and replaces the deleted Microfabrica fallback; (c) a doubled outlet header plus a 0.5 kPa outlet orifice row, which brings segment max/min from 1.36 to 1.06 at 18 LPM (re-run in final_segbal.py); (d) a mandatory supplied 33 um tray cartridge.

Plate dP is restated as 7.6 kPa (external claim <= 10 kPa), compared at matched boundaries: 2.7x at 20 mm bores, 1.7x at 12 mm. UQD08 pair is 14-24 kPa from vendor Cv; tray loop is 42-51 vs 56-79 kPa. Ratings are capped at 19.5 kW by meter velocity. The 16 mm port option is dropped.
A full OCP flow sweep was added with the CoolIT-like model patched (ramp = 0.5 dT_out, recalibrated to 119 cm2). It exposes a new concession: the average is lost at <= 0.5 LPM/kW.

Corrected claims: the 4 kW 'tie' becomes a loss for the drop-in core (PRISM-S4 SKU added); 100 cm2 average becomes parity/loss; 'maximum holds at every footprint' is deleted; 350 W/cm2 margin becomes ~17-20 K (P-grade ~88 C); GPU-class average becomes parity; flux rule never uses L 4 mm.

Cost is re-based on the verifier basis (silver, furnaces, dies, yield): draft US$209, Rev A US$165, C2 US$144, against a like-sized US$126 incumbent. Ramp cost is US$370-430. The 1M/yr comparison is removed. Facility value is restated (+5.5 K at P50, US$0.54-1.09 M/K, capture conditions stated). The GPU-class value case is shown to fail.

IP: the kerf design-around is stated as weak; family lists are corrected (including '906, '513, the 2012 family and TW I606224); the prior-art memo is corrected (US 5,088,005 is Ciaccio/Sundstrand); the FTO opinion moves to M4, before any US demo; US launch no earlier than 10 Sep 2028; US prototype exposure is flagged; filings 2-4 become defensive publications or trade secret.

Manufacturing: inspection re-scoped (dry He leak first, per-strip controls, lot over-proof and CT, IR before fly-cut, vacuum-bake dry, N2 ship state); kerf process defined; base blank >= 3.5-4 mm; filler routes resized; load-path table completed with tie bonded fraction 0.70.

New top-level sections and views: rack/CDU dP stack and contingent system value; controls and telemetry (fin-field dP taps, BMC drift, Redfish); serviceability; safety FMEA (leak FIT target, LM Al-exclusion, HV per IEC 62477-1, negative-pressure option); mechanical integration; transient model; coolant chemistry matrix E5c; sustainability (return temperature, heat reuse, water, CO2e, PFAS-free BOM); compliance matrix with Section 232 and landed cost by site; scale-up and supply chain; competitor table beyond CoolIT; competitor response; P&L; power electronics as the second application; test-infrastructure matrix; traceability; organisation with RACI-style roles and gate board; options analysis; 20 anticipated objections.

Statistics are pre-registered: a one-sample test against the published 34.4 K (5 plates x 3 re-mounts). Welch against CoolIT's n = 3 cannot resolve margins below 2.84 K. Worst-of-N is compared with worst-of-N.

Budget completed to US$8.4-10.7 M for 12 months with contingency (18 FTE, 40 kW rig, five TTVs, Build-B dies moved forward). Programme risk is now deducted from the probabilities (decisive PCM 0.43; paste average 0.58).
remaining_concessions: Per-plate factory cost: US$165 vs ~US$126 like-sized (+31 %), or +14 % with C2. This is irreducible: P(C2 <= incumbent) = 0.08.

Average at a 100 cm2 footprint with paste: 34.7 vs 34.4 K, i.e. parity or a slight loss (P 0.44). The paste maximum at 100 cm2 is not robust (P 0.57). Only the filtration-gated R+ grade or LM wins there.
Average R at low flow: lost by 17 % at 0.25 LPM/kW, parity at 0.5 LPM/kW (isothermal-cell caloric penalty). The maximum still wins at every flow.
CoolIT 4 kW point: the drop-in core loses on PCM (0.0095) and paste (0.0107). Only LM or the dedicated PRISM-S4 SKU wins, and not like-for-like until a head-to-head test.
Not fully drop-in: needs the supplied tray filter cartridge, keyed orifices in mixed racks, and <= 33 um filtration for R+/P.
Fouling exclusion life at equal filtration: ~7 y vs ~15 y for a 0.2 mm gap. Only a dose-qualified claim is possible at launch.
The system-level dP value is contingent: 6-18 % of loop head in homogeneous racks, zero in mixed racks.
GPU-class uniform lids: average at parity only, and per-plate cost higher (lean PRISM-G US$129-148 vs ~US$110). Not a value case.
350 W/cm2 over whole dies: no drop-in grade reaches 85 C (R ~98 C, P ~88 C, with LM).
The thin base gives up to 1.0 K larger excursion within 100 ms under power pulses, although the absolute peak stays lower.
US sales are IP-gated until about Sep 2028, or later if '330 PTA applies, unless the opinion clears earlier. Taiwan manufacture is blocked until TW I606224 is charted.
decisions: D1 claim scope: adopt the scoped like-for-like claim (average, maximum, uniformity, capacity, headroom; maximum at every OCP flow; dP below any credible reconstruction; lower height, parity-or-better mass, parity cost per kW; costs more per plate, ships with tray filter, no field record). Release it only after G2. Do not claim the 4 kW point, the low-flow average or the 100 cm2 average.

D2 channel: build-and-supply through a non-Group-A contract manufacturer to hyperscaler ASIC programmes first. Approach NVIDIA through its thermal engineering team, with an MCL co-design path. A licence-only route does not close.
D3 budget: fund in tranches, US$2.3 M to G1 (M3), then full scope at US$8.4-10.7 M for 12 months (US$11.4-14.5 M to M18). The lean alternative is ~US$8.3 M.
D4 Rev A stack: the Rev A vacuum-BAg baseline (US$165). Decide the C2 Cu-Sn TLP belt route (US$144) at G1 on E1 results. Retire the draft geometry.

D5 US launch and site: no US offers, sales or evaluation units before the FTO opinion at M4; no US sale before 10 Sep 2028 unless the opinion clears earlier. The build site is set by a CBP binding ruling on Section 232: Vietnam or Mexico CM first; a US second source if loose plates draw 25-50 % duty; Taiwan only after TW I606224 is charted.
D6 filtration: make the >= 150 cm2, 33 um absolute tray cartridge mandatory and supplied. Market the plate as 'mechanically drop-in, ships with tray filter kit'.
D7 hedges: US$0.4-0.6 M for an MCL-insert (T3B) design study with Jentech or AVC/Auras, plus a two-phase watching brief with defined re-entry triggers. MCL pivot decision at G2.
top_risks: R1 tie braze and per-strip detection: at a 0.8 mm base, one unbonded land strip collapses at 1.6-2.3 MPa. The base is gated on E1 proving 2.2 um bulge detection; the fallback is a 1.0 mm base (+0.7 K).

R8 IP: the Split-Flow 2008 family is live to about Sep 2028 (up to about Jun 2031 with '330 PTA), the kerf design-around is weak, TW I606224 blocks Taiwan manufacture, and Microfabrica's claim is addressed only by the stepped-grate redesign pending CFD.

R12 market: micro-channel lids and MLCP may displace lidded plates at NVIDIA from 2027, and AVC already ships TPU v8 and Trainium3 liquid cooling, so the hyperscaler beachhead is contested and volume slips to 2029.

R5/R4 benchmark: the OCP spec's recommended TIM and case definition are unread, and the footprint is ambiguous. If CoolIT's heaters were ~100 cm2 the paste average is at parity. The CoolIT-like reconstruction misses CoolIT's 4 kW datum by >= 37 %.
R9/R13 cost and tariffs: cost could exceed US$175, silver exposure is US$13-24 per plate, and Section 232 could add 0-50 % of customs value to loose plates imported into the US (CBP ruling needed).
Programme: P(decisive PCM result at M12) is about 0.43; the dominant failure mode is a 1-3 month slip at E1 or TTV commissioning.
R3 meter discharge: single-cell CFD must confirm fin-top velocity <= 0.5 m/s and the jet-on-lip geometry before the G1 freeze.
